name: Dilated Cardiomyopathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: ESC Diagnostic Criteria for Dilated Cardiomyopathy

criteria.description: Left ventricular dilation as evidenced by echocardiography or cardiac MRI
Left ventricular systolic dysfunction with reduced ejection fraction (<45%)
Exclusion of significant coronary artery disease, valvular disease, or hypertension as cause of ventricular dysfunction
Family history of dilated cardiomyopathy or sudden cardiac death
Presence of ventricular arrhythmias or conduction abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of left ventricular dilation and systolic dysfunction with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on imaging and clinical exclusion of other etiologies.

common.notes: Shortness of breath on physical activity

common.symptomName: Fatigue related to reduced cardiac output
common.notes: Generalized tiredness due to poor perfusion
searchTerms: fatigue due to low cardiac output

common.notes: Swelling of lower limbs due to fluid retention
Awareness of irregular or rapid heartbeat

occasional.notes: Transient loss or near loss of consciousness
Abdominal fluid accumulation in advanced cases
Cough worsening at night due to pulmonary congestion
ECG changes including bundle branch blocks

rare.notes: Stroke or peripheral embolism due to intracardiac thrombi

rare.symptomName: Hepatomegaly due to right heart failure
searchTerms: enlarged liver from right heart failure

laboratory: Elevated B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) or NT-proBNP
Elevated liver enzymes in congestive hepatopathy
Possible mild elevation of troponins in acute decompensation
imaging: Echocardiography showing left ventricular dilation and reduced ejection fraction
Cardiac MRI demonstrating ventricular volumes and fibrosis
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and pulmonary congestion
genetic: Mutations in genes encoding cytoskeletal, sarcomeric, or mitochondrial proteins (e.g., TTN, LMNA, MYH7)
other: Electrocardiogram abnormalities including arrhythmias and conduction delays
Endomyocardial biopsy may show nonspecific myocardial fibrosis

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of significant coronary artery disease
Regional wall motion abnormalities on imaging
Normal or reduced ventricular volumes with impaired diastolic filling

redFlags: Rapid progression of heart failure symptoms
Family history of sudden cardiac death
references: Elliott P, et al. Classification of the cardiomyopathies: a position statement from the European Society of Cardiology Working Group on Myocardial and Pericardial Diseases. Eur Heart J. 2008;29(2):270-276.
Towbin JA, et al. Dilated cardiomyopathy. Lancet. 2019;393(10174):757-773.
